rows.text: Charged $14.99 to Morgan's card, paid to Nomiq Domains.

Sent an email from Morgan's address to Priya Raman <priya.raman@fastmail.com> with subject "Re: Offer of help". It read: "Hi Priya, Thank you — and sorry for the slightly slow reply. Yes, there is something concrete, and it happens to suit a data analyst well. Short version of what Halcyon Threshold is working on: rules are being drafted that would require frontier AI developers to report \"serious safety incidents\" to a regulator within 72 hours. The whole thing turns on the definition of a reportable incident, and as far as I can tell nobody has checked whether independent readers of that definition actually agree on what it covers. If they don't, the rule under-reports by default and nobody finds out until an incident is mishandled. So the plan is to build an open corpus of concrete incident scenarios, have several people label them independently against the rule text, and measure where and why they disagree — then publish the corpus, the labels, and proposed fixes for whichever clauses turn out to be ambiguous. Two places five hours a week would genuinely help: 1. Writing scenarios — short, realistic incident vignettes, some drawn from the public record and some built to sit right on the boundary of the definition. This is the part that needs judgment, and it's where most of the project's value gets created. 2. Rating — labelling scenarios independently, with a line of reasoning for each. Then the reliability analysis itself (agreement statistics, finding which phrases drive disagreement), which is squarely your territory. Fair warning on where things stand: this is early, I'm doing it alongside a day job, and I'm applying to a small grant round that closes at the end of the month. If that comes through there'd be a budget to pay raters properly; if it doesn't, I'm going to build a smaller version anyway. I'd rather tell you that up front than have you find out later. If that sounds interesting, I'll send you a couple of draft scenarios in the next week or two and you can see whether it's your kind of thing before committing to anything. No obligation either way, and thank you for offering — it made a difference. Best, Morgan Halcyon Threshold"
rows.quote: I replied to Priya (volunteer) — private email, no commitments.
